newsitem.title: USA: Aetrium sees R&D charge on FSA acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Aetrium sees R&D charge on FSA acquisition.

text.p: Aetrium Inc said Tuesday it expects to take a one-time charge in the second quarter to cover the in-process research and development of recently acquired Forward Systems Automation Inc.
After the charge, Aetrium said it expects FSA's operations will likely be neutral to the company's earnings per share for the final three quarters of 1997.
The FSA acquisition, valued at $6.5 million, was completed on April 1 and was recorded in the second quarter, Aetrium said.

Aetrium, which supplies technology and equipment to the semiconductor industry, reported first quarter earnings of $0.13 a share, down from $0.35 last year. The company said results were in line with expectations and reflected the recent semiconductor industry-wide slump.
"We continued to see signs of an overall improvement in market conditions," president and chief executive Joseph Levesque said.
He said revenue rose from the fourth quarter of last year, and bookings for the quarter exceeded shipments by a more than two-to-one ratio.
First quarter consolidated gross margin was 51.3 percent, down from 56.1 percent last year, reflecting lower volume and a shift in product mix, Aetrium said.
Research and development expenses were 16.6 percent of revenue, which the company said was considerably higher than it has historically targeted.
